reasoning_traces.think:
The three core primitives—True Efficiency, The Luck Layer, and The Read—are constructed from foundational statistical and probabilistic principles. True Efficiency is grounded in expected points added (EPA), a metric derived from play-by-play data that quantifies offensive and defensive performance. It is filtered to exclude garbage time and kneel plays to ensure meaningful comparisons. The Luck Layer leverages probabilistic models to compare actual versus expected turnover events, assigning categorical labels based on deviation thresholds. This layer uses nflfastR’s cp/ep family for interception probabilities and empirical fumble rates. The Read component computes a scalar edge by comparing a model-derived fair line against the market line, enabling situational reasoning about betting value. Each primitive operates under distinct but complementary assumptions: EPA excludes non-competitive plays, turnover modeling assumes stationarity in event probabilities, and the fair line reflects a calibrated predictive model. Dualities emerge in how luck and efficiency interact—efficiency measures skill, while luck captures variance. Failure modes include data drift in EPA models, misclassification in turnover expectations, and model-market divergence due to liquidity or information asymmetry.
